lessons: Do not confuse Double Chance '12' ('Team A or Team B') with 'Team or Draw' (1X/X2): '12' loses on a draw and provides zero draw protection, losing 6 times when treated as safe.
Do not routinely back Double Chance '12' at short odds (<1.35) under LOSING framework records: draws occur frequently even with squad absences.
Veto or severely downgrade 'Win to Nil — no' at <=1.25 when framework record is LOSING or TOO FEW: selections lost 4 of 7 times despite opposition absences.
Do not veto Over 1.5 goals at short odds (1.20–1.31) solely due to a LOSING framework record; use 'lower' instead (won 25 of 29).
Stop backing positive Asian Handicap cushions (+0.5 to +4.5) with negative model-to-breakeven margins: cushions frequently fail (Alaves, Excelsior, Oldham, Annecy lost).
Do not treat Under 4.5 or Under 5.5 totals as automatic safe cushions at short odds: high-variance shootouts caused multiple losses (Leverkusen, Salzburg, Altrincham).
Exercise strict caution or veto away/underdog Team Over 0.5 goals when framework record is LOSING or edge is negative (e.g. Aarhus shutout confirmed veto).
Back Team Under 3.5 or Under totals only when verified offensive suppression or heavily rotated attacks are confirmed.
Never override negative EV on short-priced selections (<=1.25) purely on high nominal handicap or goals cushion: odds-on picks require genuine positive edge.
football.summary: Replaced the flawed rule treating Double Chance '12' as draw-protected, reversed leniency on 'Win to Nil — no' after 4 losses, and stopped backing negative-edge positive Asian handicaps.

lessons: Veto 1st half totals when the identical matchup is documented in recent mistakes, regardless of an overall winning family record.
Back 1st half Unders when the total line is below 120.0 points at odds 1.90 or higher; avoid or reduce stake on Unders at 120.5 or higher.
When the framework record for a betting family is LOSING, apply a downward adjustment to the model probability and back with lower confidence at odds of 1.90 or higher.
Do not back 1st half totals at odds below 1.90 unless the model probability exceeds 0.65.
Back NBA underdog handicaps (+1.5) with lower confidence when model probability exceeds 0.58, accepting odds between 1.70 and 1.85.
Apply reduced stake and lower confidence on 1st half Over bets in NBA totals due to recent volatility and mixed results.
nba.summary: Refined lessons to maintain strict threshold rules on 1st half totals, odds minimums, and added a specific caution rule for 1st half Over bets based on recent performance.

cognitive.lesson: High-probability bets can still lose to extreme scoring outliers; ensure model risk assessment accounts for tail-risk blowouts in high-total goal lines.
Even high-probability picks face random variance; never assume a bet is guaranteed despite an 80 percent base probability.
High-probability Over 1.5 bets can still fail due to normal match variance; maintain strict risk management even on strong model signals.
High-probability double chance bets can still fail due to normal match variance; always account for inherent draw risk in football.
Do not rely on high uncalibrated model probabilities without market validation for extreme handicap lines prone to blowouts.
High-probability models still lose to expected statistical variance; always manage risk even when Over 1.5 probability reaches 79%.
High probability picks near 79 percent will still lose roughly one out of five times due to standard statistical variance.
Calibrate high-confidence probabilities carefully and avoid uncalibrated bets when market validation is unavailable.
High probability model estimates can still lose to normal match variance; maintain strict bankroll management regardless of high confidence.
